14879-the-hilltop-boys-on-lost-island.title: On Lost Island
14879-the-hilltop-boys-on-lost-island.creator: Cyril Burleigh
14879-the-hilltop-boys-on-lost-island.description: A book by Cyril Burleigh. The boys belonged to the Hilltop Academy, situated in the Highlands of the Hudson, and their names were Billy Manners, Harry Dickson, and Arthur Warren, all being close chums, and ready to share any adventure except that of being seasick.

42596-the-last-call-a-romance-vol-2-of-3.title: A Romance.
42596-the-last-call-a-romance-vol-2-of-3.creator: Unknown
42596-the-last-call-a-romance-vol-2-of-3.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. "Nonsense, child," he said. "You cannot be without money in London. There is more where that came from. If you wish to go immediately to the telegraph office, you may as well start now. I will meet you in an hour at Ludgate Circus."

arxiv-2009-01896.title: Author Mentions in Science News Reveal Widespread Disparities Across Name-inferred Ethnicities
arxiv-2009-01896.creator: Hao Peng, Misha Teplitskiy, David Jurgens
arxiv-2009-01896.description: Abstract Media outlets play a key role in spreading scientific knowledge to the general public and raising the profile of researchers among their peers. Yet, how journalists choose to present researchers in their stories is poorly understood. Using a comprehensive dataset of 223,587 news stories from 288 U.S.

arxiv-2012-08824.title: Learning to Run with Potential-Based Reward Shaping and Demonstrations from Video Data
arxiv-2012-08824.creator: Aleksandra Malysheva, Daniel Kudenko, Aleksei Shpilman
arxiv-2012-08824.description: Abstract Learning to produce efficient movement behaviour for humanoid robots from scratch is a hard problem, as has been illustrated by the ”Learning to run” competition at NIPS 2017. The goal of this competition was to train a two-legged model of a humanoid body to run in a simulated race course with maximum speed.

arxiv-2102-02851.title: Dirichlet Series Expansions of p-adic L-Functions
arxiv-2102-02851.creator: Heiko Knospe, Lawrence C. Washington
arxiv-2102-02851.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Heiko Knospe, Lawrence C. Washington. We study p p -adic L L -functions L p ​ ( s , χ ) L_{p}(s,\chi) for Dirichlet characters χ \chi . We show that L p ​ ( s , χ ) L_{p}(s,\chi) has a Dirichlet series expansion for each regularization parameter c c that is prime to p p and the conductor of χ \chi .

arxiv-2105-14640.title: On some invariants of Birkhoff billiards under conjugacy
arxiv-2105-14640.creator: V. Kaloshin, C. E. Koudjinan
arxiv-2105-14640.description: Abstract In the class of strictly convex smooth boundaries, each of which not having strip around its boundary foliated by invariant curves, we prove that the Taylor coefficients of the ”normalized” Mather’s β \beta –function are invariants under C ∞ C^{\infty} –conjugacies.

arxiv-2204-06036.title: Bag breakup of low viscosity drops in the presence of a continuous air jet
arxiv-2204-06036.creator: V. Kulkarni, P. E. Sojka
arxiv-2204-06036.description: Abstract This work examines the breakup of a single drop of various low viscosity fluids as it deforms in the presence of continuous horizontal air jet. Such a fragmentation typically occurs after the bulk liquid has disintegrated upon exiting the atomizer and is in the form of an ensemble of drops which undergo further breakup.

arxiv-2303-01004.title: Mechanical cryocooler noise observed in the ground testing of the Resolve X-ray microcalorimeter onboard XRISM Journal: Journal of Low Temperature Physics
arxiv-2303-01004.creator: R. Imamura, H. Awaki, M. Tsujimoto, S. Yamada, F. S. Porter, C. A. Kilbourne, R. L. Kelley, Y. Takei, on behalf of the XRISM Resolve team
arxiv-2303-01004.description: Abstract Low-temperature detectors often use mechanical coolers as part of the cooling chain in order to reach sub-Kelvin operating temperatures. The microphonics noise caused by the mechanical coolers is a general and inherent issue for these detectors. We have observed this effect in the ground test data obtained with the Resolve instrument to be flown on the XRISM satellite.

arxiv-2305-13931.title: Position Bias Estimation with Item Embedding for Sparse Dataset Conference: Companion Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2024; May 13–17, 2024; Singapore, Singapore. Companion Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2024 (WWW ’24 Companion), May 13–17, 2024, Singapore, Singapore ISBN: 979-8-4007-01
arxiv-2305-13931.creator: Shion Ishikawa, Yun Ching Liu, Young-joo Chung, Yu Hirate
arxiv-2305-13931.description: Abstract . Estimating position bias is a well-known challenge in Learning to Rank (L2R). Click data in e-commerce applications, such as targeted advertisements and search engines, provides implicit but abundant feedback to improve personalized rankings. However, click data inherently includes various biases like position bias.

arxiv-2402-14567.title: CesASMe and Staticdeps: static detection of memory-carried dependencies for code analyzers
arxiv-2402-14567.creator: Théophile Bastian, Hugo Pompougnac, Alban Dutilleul, Fabrice Rastello
arxiv-2402-14567.description: Abstract . A variety of code analyzers, such as IACA , uiCA , llvm-mca or Ithemal , strive to statically predict the throughput of a computation kernel. Each analyzer is based on its own simplified CPU model reasoning at the scale of a basic block.

arxiv-2503-08427.title: Accelerated Distributed Optimization with Compression and Error Feedback
arxiv-2503-08427.creator: Yuan Gao, Anton Rodomanov, Jeremy Rack, Sebastian U. Stich
arxiv-2503-08427.description: Abstract Modern machine learning tasks often involve massive datasets and models, necessitating distributed optimization algorithms with reduced communication overhead. Communication compression, where clients transmit compressed updates to a central server, has emerged as a key technique to mitigate communication bottlenecks.

arxiv-2506-22372.title: Towards Fair Rankings: Leveraging LLMs for Gender Bias Detection and Measurement Conference: Proceedings of the 2025 International ACM SIGIR Conference on Innovative Concepts and Theories in Information Retrieval (ICTIR); July 18, 2025; Padua, Italy Proceedings of the 2025 International ACM SIGIR Co
arxiv-2506-22372.creator: Maryam Mousavian, Zahra Abbasiantaeb, Mohammad Aliannejadi, Fabio Crestani
arxiv-2506-22372.description: Abstract . The presence of social biases in NLP ( NLP ) and IR ( IR ) systems is an ongoing challenge, which underlines the importance of developing robust approaches to identifying and evaluating such biases. In this paper, we aim to address this issue by leveraging LLM to detect and measure gender bias in passage ranking.

arxiv-2508-07450.title: Health Care Waste Classification Using Deep Learning Aligned with Nepal's Bin Color Guidelines
arxiv-2508-07450.creator: Suman Kunwar, Prabesh Rai
arxiv-2508-07450.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Suman Kunwar, Prabesh Rai. The increasing number of Health Care facilities in Nepal has added up the challenges on managing health care waste (HCW). Improper segregation and disposal of HCW leads to contamination, spreading of infectious diseases and risk for waste handlers. This study benchmarks the state of the art waste classification models: ResNeXt-50, EfficientNet-B0, MobileNetV3-S, YOLOv8-n and YOLOv5-s using stratified 5-fold cross-validation technique on combined HCW data.

arxiv-2508-17275.title: Deep Learning–Assisted Detection of Sarcopenia in Cross-Sectional Computed Tomography Imaging
arxiv-2508-17275.creator: Manish Bhardwaj, Huizhi Liang, Ashwin Sivaharan Sandip Nandhra, Vaclav Snasel, Tamer El-Sayed, Varun Ojha
arxiv-2508-17275.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Manish Bhardwaj, Huizhi Liang, Ashwin Sivaharan Sandip Nandhra, Vaclav Snasel, Tamer El-Sayed, Varun Ojha. Sarcopenia is a progressive loss of muscle mass and function linked to poor surgical outcomes such as prolonged hospital stays, impaired mobility, and increased mortality. Although it can be assessed through cross-sectional imaging by measuring skeletal muscle area (SMA), the process is time-consuming and adds to clinical workloads, limiting timely detection and management; however, this process could become more efficient and scalable with the assistance of artificial intelligence applications.

arxiv-2510-20201.title: Asymptotics for Anisotropic Rabi Models
arxiv-2510-20201.creator: Masao Hirokawa, Fumio Hiroshima, DongYun LEE
arxiv-2510-20201.description: Abstract A one-parameter family of self-adjoint operators interpolating between the quantum Rabi Hamiltonian and its rotating-wave approximation is studied. A mathematically rigorous treatment of such interpolations has been lacking. Motivated by the physical claim that counter-rotating terms dominate at strong coupling, we analyze the limit in which the coupling constant of the anisotropic Rabi model tends to infinity.

arxiv-2511-01564.title: An Adaptive Flux Reconstruction Scheme for Robust Shock Capturing Journal: Journal of Computational Physics
arxiv-2511-01564.creator: Sai Shruthi Srinivasan, Siva Nadarajah
arxiv-2511-01564.description: Abstract 1 Introduction In the case of hyperbolic conservation laws, high-order methods, such as the classical DG method, experience the phenomenon of unwanted high-frequency oscillations in the vicinity of a shock. Shock-capturing methods such as artificial dissipation, solution, flux, or TVD limiting are generally used to eliminate nonphysical oscillations and provide bounds on physical quantities.

arxiv-2604-17481.title: A Novel Quantum Augmented Framework to Improve Microgrid Cybersecurity
arxiv-2604-17481.creator: Nitin Jha, Prateek Paudel, Abhishek Parakh, Mahadevan Subramaniam

pmc-10571866.title: Optical Genome Mapping Reveals the Complex Genetic Landscape of Myeloma
pmc-10571866.creator: Amélie Giguère, Isabelle Raymond-Bouchard, Vanessa Collin, Jean-Sébastien Claveau, Josée Hébert, Richard LeBlanc, Adam C Smith, Alex Hoischen, Gordana Raca
pmc-10571866.description: Simple SummaryMyeloma is a hematological cancer characterized by numerous genetic abnormalities currently identified using fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH). However, FISH is a targeted method offering a limited view of the genome mainly restricted to chromosomal translocations involving the IGH gene and aberrations of chromosomes 1 and 17.

pmc-10709917.title: How calling emerges and develops during COVID-19: a qualitative study of medical students
pmc-10709917.creator: Jia Xu, Baoguo Xie, Tingting Liu, Jie Li
pmc-10709917.description: IntroductionThe presence of calling in medicine has been shown to be related to a preponderance of positive outcomes among medical students. However, only a few studies examined the antecedents of calling. Of this group, little is known about how a calling emerges and develops in a crisis situation.

pmc-12615337.title: Geniposide, a potential therapeutical candidate for acute pancreatitis, inhibited trypsinogen-activated CBS degradation and remodeled transsulfuration metabolic flux
pmc-12615337.creator: Ji Gao, Yijing Long, Jiawang Li, Yiqin Wang, Rui Wang, Jinxi Yang, Jie Zhang, Chenxia Han, Qing Xia, Dan Du
pmc-12615337.description: Acute pancreatitis (AP) is a potentially fatal condition with no targeted treatment options currently available. The premature activation of trypsinogen within acinar cells constitutes one of the pivotal early pathological events in AP, contributing to oxidative stress and inflammation. Disruption of the transsulfuration pathway also plays an important role in the development of AP.

pmc-13096649.title: Dual-band graphene-assisted metamaterial absorber with machine learning integration for high-sensitivity THz biosensing
pmc-13096649.creator: Shagun Gupta, Vaishnavi Chandrashekar Gosi, Parth Pareek, Patri Upender
pmc-13096649.description: In this work, a compact dual-band terahertz (THz) metamaterial absorber integrated with graphene is presented for high-performance biosensing applications. The structure is composed of four concentric octagonal rings, where two are metallic and two are graphene-based, supported on a SiO2 substrate backed by a gold ground plane.

pmc-13145242.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026OT40 OUTCOMES OF RESCUE STENTING AND ANGIOPLASTY IN ISCHEMIC STROKE FROM A MULTICENTER RETROSPECTIVE COHORT IN RIYADH, KSA
pmc-13145242.creator: Mohammed Al Hashmi, Anas Alrohimi, Fahad Alajlan, Mohammed Aljohani, Mohammed Alshareet, Abdellah Douiri, Adel Alhazzani
pmc-13145242.description: Background and aimsMechanical thrombectomy (MT) is the standard of care for large-vessel occlusion stroke; however, 10–20% of patients experience failed or incomplete recanalization due to intracranial atherosclerotic disease, refractory thrombus, or vessel injury. In such cases, rescue stenting and/or angioplasty may restore vessel patency and improve outcomes.

pmc-13435772.description: BackgroundThe present study aims to examine the impact of badminton training programs on the attention and motor skills performance of students with specific learning disorders (SLDs).MethodsThe study was carried out with students at a public middle school. The study group consisted of a total of 44 volunteer students with SLD, with 22 participants in the experimental group (mean age 12.

pmc-13582030.title: Magnetic compression anastomosis in gastrointestinal surgery: a systematic review of early human experience
pmc-13582030.creator: Arshpreet Kaur, Samreen Shaikh, Sebastian C Valdivieso Rueda, Faran Bokhari, Vishnu R Mani
pmc-13582030.description: IntroductionMagnetic compression anastomosis (MCA) is one of the recent emerging sutureless minimally invasive techniques for maintaining the continuity of the intestine using magnetic compression. Despite its potential advantages, clinical application remains limited due to scarce evidence. The aim of this article is to review the current literature for this alternate method of bowel anastomosis.
